title: Stewardship and Mission
intro: Explore 2 Corinthians 8–9 to see how Christ's self-giving grace restores heaven's principle of receiving in order to give, making stewardship the gospel made visible in our resources.
heroQuote: Stewardship is the gospel made visible in our resources.

footer.text: For ye know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that, though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that ye through his poverty might be rich.

themes.title: Stewardship and the Circuit of Beneficence
themes.summary: Stewardship reveals which principle governs our lives: heaven's self-renouncing love or sin's self-seeking. In 2 Corinthians 8–9, God's gifts flow through believers to bless others and return to Him in thanksgiving and glory.

themes.title: Christ: The Perfect Circuit of Beneficence
themes.summary: Christ had everything, gave Himself for us, and made us rich through His poverty. His divine glory, voluntary humility, and saving mission reveal the pattern of receiving in order to give; stewardship begins with what God has already given.

quotes.quote: Christ was treated as we deserve, that we might be treated as He deserves. He was condemned for our sins, in which He had no share, that we might be justified by His righteousness, in which we had no share. He suffered the death which was ours, that we might receive the life which was His. “With His stripes we are healed. By His life and His death, Christ has achieved even more than recovery from the ruin wrought through sin. It was Satan’s purpose to bring about an eternal separation between God and man; but in Christ we become more closely united to God than if we had never fallen. In taking our nature, the Saviour has bound Himself to humanity by a tie that is never to be broken. Through the eternal ages He is linked with us. “God so loved the world, that He gave His only-begotten Son.” John 3:16. He gave Him not only to bear our sins, and to die as our sacrifice; He gave Him to the fallen race. To assure us of His immutable counsel of peace, God gave His only-begotten Son to become one of the human family, forever to retain His human nature.
quotes.author: Ellen White

themes.title: “Enriched... Unto All Bountifulness” — The Circuit Explicitly Described
themes.summary: God supplies and multiplies the seed, enabling believers to be generous. Their service meets the needs of others and produces thanksgiving to God, completing the circuit of beneficence: God gives, His people share, and gratitude returns to Him.

themes.title: Grace Starts the Circuit
themes.summary: God takes the initiative in salvation and generosity: His goodness leads to repentance, He gives faith, and His love awakens ours. Every gift comes from Him, including our ability to give; grace received becomes grace reproduced and extended to others.

themes.title: Stewardship Exposes the Governing Principle of the Heart
themes.summary: Giving does not purchase God's favor; it reveals the sincerity of our love and what governs our hearts. Through willing, cheerful generosity, God invites us to become like Him, allowing His blessings to flow to others and cultivating delight in self-renouncing love.

themes.title: Stewardship as Cosmic Witness
themes.summary: God intends Christ's self-giving mind to be reproduced in His people. Stewardship makes the gospel visible in our resources and reveals God's character to the world, calling us to ask whether His blessings are terminating with us or flowing through us.
